entities.name: Premature reproductive senescence
observations: In female rats, severe prenatal maternal undernutrition can produce an accelerated reproductive-aging phenotype with persistent estrus, ovarian follicle loss or atresia, cystic ovarian change, and altered gonadotropin-steroid signaling.
Evidence is not uniform: one gestational-restriction study found altered KNDy neuroendocrine programming without abnormal adult estrous cyclicity or LH pulsatility.

entities.name: PMID:25439841
observations: Late-gestation maternal food restriction in Sprague-Dawley rats was followed by disrupted estrous cycles in 80% of female offspring by 8 months, mostly persistent estrus, with cystic ovarian structures, fewer corpora lutea, increased LH/FSH and testosterone, and reduced estradiol; AMH was unchanged.

entities.name: PMID:29351580
observations: Maternal intake at 50% of control during pregnancy caused persistent-estrus irregular cycles, fewer antral follicles and corpora lutea, more atretic follicles, and increased ovarian CASP3 in female offspring at postnatal day 65.

entities.name: PMID:25810471
observations: Pregnancy, pregnancy-plus-lactation, or lactation-only 50% caloric restriction was associated in adult female offspring with fewer ovarian follicles, increased ovarian ER stress and follicular apoptosis, and reduced ovarian vessel density, interpreted as accelerated ovarian aging.

entities.name: PMID:36408965
observations: Maternal food restriction to 50% from gestational day 9 to term caused low birth weight, precocious puberty, and altered KNDy-cell measures, but adult estrous cyclicity and pulsatile LH secretion remained comparable with controls through the reported follow-up.

entities.name: Prenatal restriction phenotype
observations: The strongest direct evidence supports accelerated reproductive aging rather than proven permanent infertility: persistent estrus and ovarian pathology occur early, while exact age at irreversible reproductive cessation and adult fecundity are usually not measured.
